Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro today. As we discussed, Launchly is planning a phased public launch in Q2 with a small beta (10k monthly tokens) in April, then a staged ramp across two larger markets in May/June that could triple usage in the first month after full launch. We expect heavy seasonality spikes during promotions (campaign windows) roughly 2-3x baseline for 48-72 hours.

Our ask: we want a predictable per-token rate while preserving flexibility for the initial months. Specifically: can Redwood support a month-1 lower-commit floor that steps up over three monthly tiers, with a burst pool or surge credits for short spikes? We want clarity on:
- how overage is billed vs true-up options
- what surge protection looks like (credits vs temporary burst capacity)
- any minimums that lock in pricing tiers

Maya —

Thanks for the deck and the traffic worksheet. This looks like a classic launcher pattern (small beta -> rapid step-up) and we have a couple of options that most customers use:

1) Staircase commit: a three-step monthly commit where you commit to a lower bucket in month 1, a higher bucket in month 2, and full target in month 3. Each tier has a per-token blended discount that improves as you step up. We include a 14-day buffer for short ingress differences and a single true-up at the end of the quarterly period.

2) Commit + surge pool: committed tokens cover baseline and steady ramp; we maintain a small burst pool (pre-purchased credits) that apply automatically during short promotions. Any additional overage beyond pool is billed at an overage rate or can be true-upped to next commit tier.

I've sketched a high-level staircase proposal and attached it (redwood-staircase-proposal.pdf). The doc includes suggested bucket sizes given your numbers, a sample blended per-token rate, and two surge-credit options (prepaid pool vs. dynamic credits applied as discounts).

Quick asks from our side to firm this up:
- confirm which months are your campaign windows (so we size the burst pool)
- confirm whether you prefer prepaid burst credits or a carry-forward true-up model
- any hard invoice timing / procurement constraints for net-30 vs net-45

Would Marissa or I schedule a 30-minute call to walk the materials on Thursday?

Ben / Maya — great notes. Picking up from Irene's options, here's an alternative structure that other customers have liked for launch programs:

Proposal (high level)
- Month 1: onboarding bucket (lower per-token commit) — protects you as you ramp product/UX.
- Month 2: intermediate bucket (50% increase) — reduced per-token price vs M1.
- Month 3+: target commit (full rate) with monthly true-up.
- Smoothing ladder: we add a +/- 10% corridor where if actual usage falls within 10% below the next tier, we keep the higher-tier per-token price for that month (no cliff). This avoids punishing close misses.
- Burst credits: two sub-options:
  a) Prepaid pool sized to cover 1.5x average campaign spike; unspent credits carry forward for 3 months.
  b) Dynamic surge credits: we allow short auto-burst up to a fixed threshold and charge at an overage rate which is discounted if you elect to true-up within the quarter.

Billing notes (finance): we can do net-30. For larger prepayments, we can invoice 50% up front for the staircase and the remainder on first true-up.

Next steps:
1) Rishi (cc'd) will confirm the exact billing cadence and any enterprise approval steps.
2) If you like the smoothing ladder, we will update the proposal PDF with explicit numbers and an example invoice.

Looping in a couple finance considerations so expectations are clear before contract stage:

- Invoice cadence: For staircase commitments we prefer 30-day invoicing, with an option to invoice 50% upfront for the entire staircase to secure capacity during launch windows.
- True-up mechanics: any overage can be either invoiced at the overage rate or applied as a true-up credit to the next month's commitment; customers must elect true-up within the quarter for the discount to apply.
- Burst pool accounting: prepaid burst credits are refundable only if the total contract is canceled before first full quarter; otherwise carry-forward policy applies as Marissa described.
- SLA exception: Launchly asked for a 99.9% latency SLO for the first 6 weeks of launch. That SLO is above our standard hosted tier. Legal will need to review; procurement should expect additional SLA language and a possible pricing uplift tied to the SLO.

I've attached a redlined billing cadence doc that maps invoice flows and sample numbers (redwood-billing-cadence-redline.docx).
